name: v1_zero_rates_baseline_renter_invests
derivation: Fully hand-enumerable, zero everything. Loan = 120,000×0.8 = 96,000 at 0% over 24 months → payment = 96,000/24 = 4,000/mo. Owner cost 4,000 vs rent 3,000 → renter invests 1,000/mo × 24 = 24,000 at 0% growth. Renter seed = down payment 24,000 + closing 0 − deposit 0 = 24,000 → portfolio 48,000 = rentNW (no CGT: 0% return). Buy: balance after 24 payments = 0, home value 120,000, no selling costs/taxes → buyNW = 120,000. Conservation check: both sides outlaid 24,000 + 96,000 + 72,000 rent-equivalent... buyer total cash 120,000 → owns 120,000 home; renter total cash 120,000 → 72,000 rent burned + 48,000 portfolio. Break-even year 1: liquidation y1 buy = 120,000 − 48,000 = 72,000 > renter 24,000+12,000 = 36,000. The current repo engine agrees on this vector (no defect triggered) — it anchors that the corrected engine only diverges where defects exist.

name: v2_buyer_surplus_must_be_invested
derivation: Tests defect D01 (one-directional investing). Loan = 60,000 at 0% over 300 months → payment 200/mo. Owner cost 200 < rent 1,000 → BUYER invests 800/mo × 24 = 19,200 (0% growth). Renter seed = down 60,000, no contributions → 60,000 = rentNW. Balance after 24 mo = 60,000 − 4,800 = 55,200; equity = 120,000 − 55,200 = 64,800. buyNW = 64,800 + 19,200 = 84,000. Break-even 1: y1 buy = (120,000 − 57,600) + 9,600 = 72,000 > 60,000. Current repo engine returns buyNW = 64,800 — drops the entire 19,200 buyer portfolio.

name: v3_horizon_beyond_term_payment_stops
derivation: Tests defect D03 (horizon > term). Loan 60,000, 0%, 12 months → payment 5,000/mo, paid off at end of year 1; totalInterest must be exactly 0. Year 1: owner 5,000 > rent 2,000 → renter invests 3,000×12 = 36,000; renter = 60,000 seed + 36,000 = 96,000. Years 2–3: owner cost 0 → buyer invests 2,000×24 = 48,000. buyNW = 120,000 home + 48,000 = 168,000; rentNW = 96,000; buy wins by 72,000. Current repo engine inverts the verdict: it keeps charging the 5,000 payment for years 2–3, books 120,000 phantom interest on a 0% loan, credits the renter 3,000/mo for 36 months → reports buy 120,000 vs rent 168,000 (rent 'wins' by 48,000) with breakEvenYear null.

name: v4_cash_purchase_100pct_down
derivation: Tests defect D05: the current engine throws 'Loan amount must be greater than 0'. Correct behavior: loan = 0, payment = 0, no interest, no PMI, mortgageInterestRate/mortgageTerm irrelevant. Owner cost 0 < rent 1,000 → buyer invests 1,000×24 = 24,000 (0% growth). buyNW = 100,000 home + 24,000 = 124,000. Renter seed = 100,000 (the buyer's full cash price) → rentNW = 100,000. Buy wins by exactly the rent avoided (24,000) since all rates are 0.

name: v6_pmi_cancellation_original_value_monthly
derivation: PMI convention test (spec: charged in month m iff start-of-month balance > 80% of ORIGINAL price; 0% appreciation makes original-value and current-value bases coincide, isolating the monthly-evaluation convention). Loan = 90,000 at 0% over 120 mo → payment 750/mo; start-of-month-m balance = 90,000 − 750(m−1) > 80,000 ⟺ m ≤ 14 (m=14: 80,250 > 80,000; m=15: 79,500). PMI = 1%×90,000/12 = 75/mo × 14 months = 1,050. Owner cost months 1–14 = 825 vs rent 1,200 → buyer invests 375; months 15–24 → 450. Buyer portfolio = 14×375 + 10×450 = 9,750 (0% growth). Balance after 24 mo = 72,000; equity = 28,000. buyNW = 28,000 + 9,750 = 37,750. Renter = seed 10,000 → 10,000. (Current engine: 900 PMI — full year 1 charged from end-of-year state, year 2 waived retroactively — and buyNW 28,000 with the buyer portfolio dropped.)

name: v8_section121_excess_gain_selling_costs_in_basis
derivation: Section 121 with amount-realized/basis correctness (D11) on a cash purchase (D05). Home value after 1 year = 2,000,000×1.20 = 2,400,000; selling costs = 6% = 144,000. Taxable gain = (2,400,000 − 144,000) − 2,000,000 = 256,000; minus $250,000 single exclusion → 6,000 taxable × 15% = 900 tax. Owner cost 0 → buyer invests 5,000×12 = 60,000 (0% growth). buyNW = 2,400,000 − 144,000 − 900 + 60,000 = 2,315,100. Renter seed 2,000,000, 0% return → 2,000,000. (Current engine: throws on 100% down; and its gain formula HV − price = 400,000 → tax 22,500, overstating by 21,600.)

name: v9_compounding_rent_growth_annuity_closed_form
derivation: Verifies contribution timing (end-of-month), monthly rate = 6%/12 = 0.5%, year-boundary rent escalation with (y−1) exponent, and portfolio CGT with basis tracking — all by annuity closed forms. Payment = 240,000/360 = 666.67 (exactly 2,000/3). Owner cost 666.67 < rent → buyer invests: year 1 c1 = 2,000 − 2,000/3 = 4,000/3 = 1,333.33/mo; year 2 rent = 2,200 → c2 = 1,533.33/mo. Ordinary-annuity factor s = (1.005^12 − 1)/0.005 = 12.3355622; growth factor g12 = 1.005^12 = 1.0616778. Buyer portfolio = c1·s·g12 + c2·s = 16,447.42×1.0616778 + 18,914.53 = 17,461.86 + 18,914.53 = 36,376.39; basis = 12(c1 + c2) = 34,400 → CGT = 0.15×1,976.39 = 296.46. Renter portfolio = 60,000×1.005^24 = 60,000×1.1271598 = 67,629.59; basis 60,000 → CGT = 0.15×7,629.59 = 1,144.44 → rentNW = 66,485.15. Home equity = 300,000 − (240,000 − 24×666.67) = 76,000 → buyNW = 76,000 + 36,376.39 − 296.46 = 112,079.93.

derivation: Computed with an independent reference implementation written directly from this spec (scratchpad/refspec.mjs), cross-checked at every step against closed forms: (1) Payment on 400,000 at 6.5%/30y = 400,000×(0.0054167×1.0054167^360)/(1.0054167^360−1) = 2,528.27 — matches standard amortization tables. (2) Year-1 interest 25,868.36 via B12 closed form (B12 = 395,529.10). (3) Year-1 tax benefit: SALT = min(5,500, 40,400) = 5,500; avg balance 397,765 < 750k → full interest deductible; benefit = (25,868.36 + 5,500 − 16,100)×0.24 = 3,664.41 → credit 305.37/mo. (4) Year-1 owner cost = 2,528.27 + 458.33 (tax) + 208.33 (ins) + 200 (HOA) + 416.67 (maint) − 305.37 = 3,506.23 vs renter 2,520 → renter invests 986.23/mo; owner remains dearer all 10 years so buyerPortfolio stays 0. (5) Renter seed = 100,000 + 12,500 − 2,500 = 110,000; monthly growth (7 − 0.05)/1200; end-of-month contributions; Vr(10y) = 361,254.67, basis 205,213.94 → CGT 23,406.11 → rentNW = 337,848.56 + 2,500 deposit = 340,348.56. (6) buyNW = 500,000×1.03^10 (= 671,958.19) − 339,104.51 − 40,317.49 (6% selling) − 0 (gain 131,641 − selling costs < 250k exclusion) = 292,536.19. (7) Verified results are bit-identical with dividendYield 0 vs 1.3 (total-return convention). Renting wins by ≈ 47,800 over 10 years at these conservative defaults; break-even null.
